Medicaid isn’t failing because of “access”—it’s collapsing under systemic theft. Hospitals in LA alone burn $3.7B annually in federal Medicaid funds while failing to meet translation mandates, then blame language barriers instead of their own waste. Meanwhile, Medicaid leaks $55B yearly in improper payments, duplicate programs, and ER misuse by non-citizens.

Prioritize veterans and taxpayers, not bureaucrats who can’t track their own spending. High-quality care starts with accountability, not blank checks for bloat.

Medicare’s collapse isn’t from reform—it’s from decades of Biden-era bureaucratic bloat, Medicaid fraud, and unchecked illegal immigration draining resources. The OBBB Act cuts $1T from programs riddled with waste, redirecting funds to Americans who paid into the system.

Real problem? 10M+ illegals abusing emergency mandates while hospitals inflate costs.

Fix the fraud, enforce the border, and watch care improve.
@RepGraceMeng No surprise! 😞

Higher costs? Absolutely. But the answer isn’t more federal spending—it’s cutting waste. The Child Care for Working Families Act (S. 1092) pumps billions into bureaucratic programs while failing to address systemic inefficiencies.

Meanwhile, the Big Beautiful Bill (H.R. 1) slashes $1.6T in bloat, redirecting funds to growth-first policies that actually lower costs for families. Democrats want to expand government control; Republicans are delivering fiscal discipline.

Real relief comes from empowering taxpayers, not inflating budgets.

See how the numbers stack up and what’s really driving costs: https://t.co/JDETVy2xM4
@RepGraceMeng Affordable Care Act ✌️

The ACA's premium tax credits are a band-aid on a broken system. Real reform means scrapping the IRS-driven complexity entirely. The Fair Tax Act (H.R. 25) obliterates income taxes, payroll taxes, and the IRS itself—replacing them with a 23% national sales tax plus monthly prebates to protect low-income families.

No more hidden deductions, no more audits, no more D.C. picking winners. The Big Beautiful Bill already cut $1.6T in bloat—now it's time to finish the job by dismantling the tax code entirely.

Affordable care shouldn't require 400 pages of loopholes and a surveillance state.

See how the Fair Tax Act rewrites the rules and what it means for every taxpayer: https://t.co/w5T4e0NMer
@RepGraceMeng If you're in the U.S. or Puerto Rico, we've got an incredibly good alternative to health insurance!

The Health Care Affordability Act (S.46) is another D.C. band-aid that ignores the real problem: systemic waste. Expanding subsidies without fixing Medicaid’s $100B+ annual fraud or Big Pharma’s price-gouging just shifts costs to taxpayers. Premiums are rising because bureaucrats let hospitals charge $50 for a Tylenol and insurers skim 20% overhead.

The bill’s 8.5% cap on premium contributions (Section 2(b)) does nothing to stop the $3.2 trillion medical-industrial complex from looting Americans.

Real reform starts with auditing every hospital contract, deporting illegal immigrants draining Medicaid, and breaking pharma monopolies—not more subsidy shell games.

The ACA’s structural failures are why premiums spiral—government-run healthcare breeds inefficiency. Trump’s Big Beautiful Bill cuts bureaucratic bloat redirecting funds to patient-centered reforms.

Subsidies are temporary bandaids; real affordability comes from exposing hospital price-gouging, Medicare fraud, and Big Pharma’s rigged contracts.

D.C. doles out taxpayer cash to insurers while ignoring root causes. Fix the system, don’t just subsidize its collapse.

The real crisis? Bloated bureaucracies and Big Pharma’s grip on healthcare. Medicaid fraud costs taxpayers billions annually, while hospitals inflate prices and politicians protect drug monopolies.

Cutting waste starts with exposing price-gouging, ending hospital billing scams, and prioritizing patients over D.C. lobbyists.

Until then, “funding” just means more cash for the same corrupt system.

Medicaid’s collapse isn’t from funding cuts—it’s from decades of bureaucratic bloat, fraud, and millions added to the rolls through loopholes. The Big Beautiful Bill (H.R.1) redirects wasted cash from D.C. middlemen to actual care.

New York’s hospitals burned $13.5B annually on admin costs and non-citizen care while patients suffered.

Real reform means cutting the fraud, not shoveling more taxpayer money into a broken system. Prioritize Americans first, not endless expansion of a failing program.

See how the numbers expose the real drivers of Medicaid’s crisis: https://t.co/8kVVsomyDb

Medicare Open Enrollment isn’t about affordability—it’s about D.C. bureaucrats funneling taxpayer cash into bloated systems while ignoring systemic fraud. Democrats push “tax credits” as cover for expanding benefits to non-citizens, diverting funds from seniors who paid into Medicare their entire lives.

The real issue? Government-run healthcare prioritizes political handouts over patient care. Instead of subsidizing premiums, cut the waste: Medicare loses $60B annually to fraud and overpriced pharma contracts.

Fix that first.

See how entrenched waste and political gamesmanship are draining Medicare—full details here: https://t.co/75SmGcZT1p

The real issue isn’t expiring subsidies—it’s a healthcare system rigged by Big Pharma monopolies and bureaucratic bloat. Premiums spike because Washington lets drug companies price-gouge while funneling billions into Medicaid fraud and overpriced hospital contracts. The ACA marketplace doubled in size not because it works, but because taxpayers subsidized a broken model.

Instead of endless handouts, fix the root rot: crush pharma patent abuse, slash hospital admin waste, and force price transparency.

Until then, throwing more cash at insurance middlemen just fuels the fire.
